sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Praruh is a fast-growing ICT systems integrator and equipment/services supplier, not yet a demonstrated proprietary software compounder. Its revenue and economic value added have genuinely expanded, and the IPO removed bank debt. The decisive concern is that FY26 growth converted into receivables and inventory rather than cash, with suppliers supplying most of the incremental funding. A related-party AI marketing agreement does not establish owned platform revenues. At the dated secondary reference of ₹139, reported earnings imply about 20.6× P/E, not an obviously distressed valuation. The conclusion is Hold — unresolved: a financing-sensitive growth watchlist, not an eligible purchase or compounder candidate. An explicit reconciliation of prior gross bank/deposit presentation, satisfactory collections and sustained funded execution would change the assessment; a cheaper quote alone would not.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Praruh Technologies Limited, BSE SME code 544538, ISIN INE0TI501017, has 13,930,000 equity shares of ₹10 face value. The official 19 October 2026 interoperability security master verifies a 2000-share lot. Its PRARUH$ SM/ST records concern exchange interoperability and do not establish an NSE listing. The eligible ST row has status 6, whose numeric meaning is not inferred without the codebook. The reference quote ₹139 is an exact 19 October secondary historical observation, not authenticated BSE tape; it gives a conditional equity value ₹193.627 crore. The financial cutoff is 20 October 2026 and audited standalone AS accounts end 31 March 2026. H1 FY27 results were not found published by cutoff. The model spans 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031, exact days divided by 365.2425, with a 15% nominal pre-personal-tax INR hurdle and 12/18% alternatives. The ₹5 lakh position is a tradability reference, not personalized sizing. Confidence is high on issuer identity and audited current line items, medium on operating growth/incremental returns, and low on the unresolved comparative gross classification, realizable timing and full market depth. G1 Conditional, G2 material Hold, G3 Conditional and G4 Conditional control the verdict.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: The canonical factor assessments are GOV5, MOAT5, REV8, DUR6, CAP7, CASH3, BAL5, EXEC6, EARN6, R NS, D4, P NS and L NS. BQS is 5.58, with complete factor coverage. Raw GQS6.65 is capped at 5.00 because persistently weak cash realization prevents rapid sales growth from being classified as high-quality compounding. IAS remains NS: its known contribution is 2.195 at 45% coverage, and raw diagnostic bounds are 2.745–7.695. Missing factors are neither filled with neutral points nor renormalized. R/P are unscored because no ordinary gate-cleared return/price model exists; L is unscored because 19 secondary sessions cannot substitute for the 60-session reference and execution restrictions. All ranking eligibility flags arefalse because of the material G2 Hold. Exact Decimal weights, raw contributions, missing bounds, HALF_UP display and a complete 9-cell CAP/DUR ±1 uncertainty grid are retained below. The scores describe evidence, not precision about future outcomes.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Customers procure integrated communications, IT infrastructure, networking, cybersecurity, audiovisual/telepresence equipment and implementation/support. Praruh specifies and sources OEM hardware, buys outside services, integrates delivery and may maintain installations. Revenue recognition is substantially project/delivery or service-performance based, not a recurring subscription automatically earned from installed software. FY26 goods revenue was ₹68.1482 crore and services ₹32.9607 crore, all domestic in that year; FY25 had a small export service amount. Externally consumed material/direct costs ₹57.8829 crore plus purchased services ₹20.7764 crore absorbed 77.80% of sales. The ₹22.4496 crore residual is an analyst value-added proxy before staff, overhead and depreciation, not audited gross profit, net revenue or ARR. Gross recognition may be appropriate where the issuer is principal, but comparing its gross sales multiple with SaaS would be economically misleading. Receivable collection, project acceptance and supplier credit determine actual cash economics. No subsidiary, acquired operating business or platform cohort was identified. Capitalized internal software ₹1.7831 crore was still under development at March 2026, with no amortization begun; software ownership and future usefulness do not yet prove monetization or recurring margins.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: The plausible advantage is public-sector/vendor qualification, technical integration skill, procurement coordination and successful mission-critical installation. These can reduce the buyer’s coordination risk and support follow-on maintenance, but OEM products and key technical intellectual property belong largely to partners. FY25’s largest customer represented 53.77% of revenue and its top 10 accounted for 98.90%; the December rating describes government customers as 75–80% of sales. Such buyers can have strong tender bargaining power and lengthy acceptance/payment cycles. Related-party WizeVerse’s AI platform is not owned by Praruh merely because it may market the product. Adtran’s contract is a supplier framework and Quantum is vendor access, not captive customer demand. Orient Technologies provides a useful listed operating comparison in infrastructure/cloud/managed services, and Allied Digital illustrates broader systems-integration and recurring-support economics. Neither licenses an automatic peer multiple for this much smaller, concentrated issuer. Better service mix may improve returns, but audited recurring-revenue retention, differentiated gross margins and contractual switching costs are not disclosed. MOAT5 recognizes useful capabilities without treating partnerships, prestigious customers or government spending as a structural monopoly.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: The preselected FY21–FY26 window contains six full annual revenue observations and five intervals. Sales increased from ₹6.85179662 crore to ₹101.1089 crore, a 71.32% CAGR. FY23–FY26 grew from ₹27.9670 crore at 53.48%. The annual additions, including FY25’s near-flat sales and FY26’s ₹39.2229 crore addition, are shown below rather than replaced by an average growth claim. The underlying value-added cross-check grew from roughly ₹1.8363 crore FY21 to ₹22.4496 crore FY26, a 65% five-year CAGR, so external procurement alone does not explain the expansion. However FY26 sales growth 63.38% translated into only 20.46% value-added growth, showing mix/procurement pressure. No acquisitions explain the standalone growth in the reviewed records; physical project volumes, unit prices and constant-currency components are not separately audited, so this is nominal organic-scope growth, not proven unit growth. FY21 sales were 14.11% below FY20’s partial incorporation period, which cannot be annualized or treated as a clean full-year pre-pandemic base. There is no arbitrary small-base penalty. The numerical REV anchor 9 is limited to 8 by medium confidence in demand decomposition and persistence, not by a second discretionary growth penalty. FY26 H1 declined and H2 supplied 82.59% of annual sales. The latest comparable half and conflicting rounded management comparative are explicitly preserved; no unreported FY27 momentum is invented.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Accessible demand consists of more qualified public-sector IT/networking deployments, additions to existing accounts and installation-linked maintenance, not a percentage of a global AI TAM. The September RailTel ₹31.2076 crore rate agreement demonstrates access but requires separate subpurchase orders; its 36-month warranty precedes five-year AMC. The full face is not guaranteed current backlog or an eight-year subscription asset. The model therefore uses conservative hypothetical revenue growth 0/15/25%, not a sum of every announced partnership. At 15%, annual turnover must more than double over five years, requiring repeated projects of meaningful size alongside retained customers. Each case funds inventory, receivables, payroll/overheads, ongoing capex and support obligations. The FY23–FY26 reported EBIT-based incremental NOPAT increase ₹7.4120 crore (₹7.1357 crore after recurring BG costs) divided by ₹29.8915 crore additional net funded capital is 23.87% after recurring BG-cost normalization, supporting CAP7 relative to an illustrative 12–16% operating capital-cost range. This is a stable standalone aggregate bridge, not a project IRR; matched ₹9.09 crore debt/deposit gross offsets do not alter its net arithmetic. An extra ₹20 crore capital requirement if supplier terms normalize reduces the same return proxy to 14.30% after the same normalization, demonstrating sensitivity. The cash investment cross-check, depreciation, WC change and ₹1.4276 crore residual are retained, with disposals/deposit/tax bases limiting precision. Software development is still uncommissioned. CASH3 therefore caps GQS at 5 despite high REV and respectable historical aggregate CAP. Required pledged deposits must also remain in operating capital. Adding FY26 operational collateral ₹2.5256 crore and bounding FY23 collateral from zero to ₹1.9845 crore produces economic incremental returns 22.01–23.45%; adding the separate ₹20 crore supplier normalization stress then gives 13.61–14.15%. These bounds still support an adequate-to-strong aggregate capital-return assessment but are not a precise project IRR.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: The three principal promoters retain around 73.22%, but control concentration is not evidence of minority-friendly capital allocation by itself. FY26 managerial remuneration to Vishal, Amar, Rahul and Pariza totals ₹1.8851 crore, about 20% of PAT; related staff and consultancy make total related-person outflows larger. FY25 remuneration of ₹1.6037 crore exceeded the ordinary statutory limit but had a shareholder special resolution, so it is not described as an illegal payment. Networkwize purchases ₹0.8661 crore and outstanding ₹0.6480 crore are material enough to track but are already inside costs/payables and must not be charged twice. The same company’s rebranding as WizeVerse is central to interpreting the AI announcement. The April 2026 encumbrance declaration states no encumbrance created during FY26; an October refresh remains unverified. Execution is mixed: the November 2025 call promised FY26 revenue above ₹90 crore and preservation of prior PBT/PAT percentages. Revenue ₹101.11 crore met the sales ambition, while PBT margin fell 14.75%→12.29% and PAT margin 10.83%→9.30%. Full auditor/CARO/IFC/edit-log conclusions are generally favorable and no default/fraud is reported. Disclosure weaknesses include the unresolved comparative gross-bank/deposit bridge and cost-record production. Prior asset reclassification/deferred-tax typography are separately bounded, not inflated into misconduct allegations.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY26 PBT ₹12.4251 crore plus finance cost ₹0.9801 crore less other income ₹0.4995 crore gives operating EBIT ₹12.9057 crore; EBITDA is ₹13.5248 crore. The normalized 25% tax operating approach gives PAT ₹8.9442 crore after financing, against reported ₹9.4067 crore. Full expensing of software WIP would reduce EBIT to ₹11.1226 crore as a sensitivity, not a claim capitalization is wrong. Reported weighted EPS ₹7.80 uses 12.065 m shares; PAT on the current 13.93 m share count is ₹6.75, so forward comparisons cannot use the pre-IPO denominator. The cash bridge is much weaker: pre-WC operating cash ₹13.3725 crore, receivables absorption ₹47.4301 crore and inventory ₹16.5850 crore were offset by ₹56.7187 crore supplier financing, leaving CFO ₹0.1328 crore and cash-capex FCF−₹1.8945 crore. Three-year CFO/PAT is 31.30%; five-year 24.96%. End-point receivable days 272.84 and supplier days 340.74 differ from average-balance 187.23 and 209.15; neither set is mislabeled as the other. Much of AR is recent Q4 billing, while ₹3.9346 crore older than one year has no provision. Bank debt is zero but trade creditors are ₹73.4321 crore. Cash ₹2.7163 crore plus free FD ₹8.9028 crore less IPO earmarks ₹5.0002 crore yields ₹6.6189 crore free. Pledged FD ₹2.5256 crore remains operational/restricted. Tax, employee and provision obligations are paid once in models; trade payables already sit in ONWC. FY25’s exact ₹9.09 crore gross asset/debt contraction lacks a specific bridge despite net cancellation, motivating G2 Hold without alleging cash disappearance. Economic operating EBIT is ₹12.5080 crore after reclassifying ₹0.3977 crore recurring BG/borrowing charges from finance cost, and economic EBITDA ₹13.1271 crore. Normalized PAT already deducts those charges, so it is not reduced twice. Forecast margins include recurring guarantee/transaction costs even when bank debt is zero.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: The correct primary valuation is a cash-funded integration earnings/enterprise-value model, not a software ARR multiple. At the ₹139 secondary dated reference and 13.93 m shares, market capitalization is ₹193.627 crore, reported P/E20.58× and normalized P/E21.65×. Using March free cash after a ₹1 crore operating reserve gives a mixed-date diagnostic EV ₹188.0081 crore and 14.32× economic EBITDA. These are not authenticated October book values. Monthly projections bridge March 2026 to the October entry and exact October 2031 exit, with FY26 low-H1/high-H2 seasonality, gradual WC transition, eligible IPO releases, old liabilities, cash tax, recurring development/maintenancecapex and stressed collection/payment timing. The bear uses 0% growth/8% EBIT margin/45% ONWC/7×terminal EBITDA; base 15%/11.5%/32%/10×; bull 25%/14%/25%/13×. Base reserve failure is modest and conditional, not proof of insolvency; bull is financeable on its assumptions. Every non-rescue return is suppressed if any reserve breach occurs, including pre-entry. Explicit hypothetical equity rescue issues whole shares at 80% of each tested price with 2% fees before uses, showing dilution instead of free funding. Even funded conditional returns are not ordinary returns under G2 Hold. Bracketed 12/15/18% entry-price and reverse-growth solvers rerun dilution at each trial. Complete joint DSO×DPO, growth×WC, capex×WC, margin×multiple, credit×interest and reserve×timing grids make the funding assumptions visible. No unsupported endpoint is relabeled a solved requirement.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The strongest credible permanent-loss chain is a concentrated government project delayed or reduced, followed by slower acceptance/collections, inventory mismatch and tighter OEM credit. Nominal sales/PAT can initially remain positive while supplier cash calls exceed realizable receivables. Guarantee invocation and adverse tax orders can compound the gap. The bear therefore combines no growth, lower margins,45% ONWC, partial tax settlement and an incremental guarantee loss rather than blindly adding the whole ₹15.59 crore guarantee face to already modeled payables. Rescue dilution and a lower terminal multiple show how an apparently profitable integrator can lose per-share value. The single most important variable is cash realization relative to supplier terms, not the number of brand partnerships. The strongest counterevidence is clean audit controls, recent Q4 AR, no bank default, debt repayment, substantial free FD cash and demonstrated revenue execution. Those positives justify Conditional funding rather than a claim of actual distress. G2 Hold is specifically the material gross-bank/deposit bridge, not a presumption every receivable is false. Persistent failure to collect older balances, supplier restrictions or unsupported revenue recognition would be stronger thesis breaks; ordinary lumpy billing alone would not.

sections.title: 5× /10× Feasibility
sections.text: A5× or 10× per-share outcome is not established by multiplying a high historical CAGR by a software multiple. Five-year price appreciation of 5× requires about 38.0% annualized and 10× about 58.5%, versus the 15% required-return reference. The retained reverse tests solve for revenue growth at 8%,11.5% and 14% EBIT margins with actual modeled WC, capex, fees, rescue shares and terminal debt/cash. They use the first bracketed crossing only within 0–100% CAGR; a missing crossing is not asserted impossible beyond the tested domain. Even a numeric solution is a demanding hypothetical, not a probability. More turnover requires larger project execution, supplier commitments and collections; a blanket RailTel rate agreement and non-guaranteed AI marketing program are not a sufficient bottom-up market-share bridge. A lower 7× terminal multiple in the bear and material margin/WC sensitivities prevent valuation expansion doing all the work. Accordingly multibagger language is speculative/unsupported on present evidence, although real organic-scope growth and meaningful incremental operating returns make the company worth monitoring.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Review the next reported half-year and annual statements, plus material operating disclosures, against the eight explicit monitoring rows below. The primary test is whether collections follow FY26 Q4 billing without creditor terms remaining at extreme end-point days. Monitor gross-bank/deposit reconciliation; aged AR receipts; supplier days and payable aging; CFO/PAT; eligible IPO use; software commissioning and external cash revenue; concentration/order conversion; and delivery versus margin promises. Warning thresholds are research triggers tied to this issuer’s baselines, not automatic buy/sell commands. In particular a base-case ₹1 crreserve assumption is not a covenant or actual minimum balance. Distinguish a late project within a seasonally weak half from a repudiated contract or unreconciled accounting item. A formal corrected comparative bridge and improving cash realization can remove specific holds; a new partner logo cannot. No recurring alert or trade has been scheduled by this research.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Hold — unresolved, research-priority/watchlist only. BQS5.58 indicates mixed business quality rather than an evidence-backed compounder. GQS is capped 5.00 by cash conversion, and IAS is NS with no permissible price-dependent classification. The company fails the compounder test because BQS isbelow 8, MOATbelow 7, CASHbelow 6, BALbelow 6 and a critical reliability gate remains open. This is not an Avoid —governance finding and not evidence of an actual funding default. The priced bullcase is conditional, the basecase requires modest financing under the chosen conservative cash-floor test, and the bear requires substantially more. An independently reconciled gross balance bridge, subsequent collections, credible supplier terms, demonstrated software/service cash economics and a validated BSE market record would permit a reassessment. Only then could a bracketed entry price become a usable price consideration rather than a conditional model diagnostic. Existing-holder portfolio actions cannot be inferred without holdings, tax and execution constraints; no transaction is contemplated here.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: The evidence register links issuer prospectus, annual reports, complete audit annexures, official results/IPOutilisation, shareholding/encumbrance filings, dated contracts, CRISIL rationale and the exact official interoperability master. Original source files were inspected but only safe analytical facts/URLs/hashes are retained in the distributable package. FY21 amounts are rupees divided by 10,000,000; later lakh figures divide by 100. CFO/PAT aggregates flows; operating EBIT removes other income; normalized earnings use 25% tax; capital comparisons retain consistent standalone scope and show residuals. Cash excludes pledged FD and all IPO earmarks before eligible uses are released. Historical source differences, the unmodified-but-emphasized FY25 matters, and the FY26 deferred-tax sign are explained rather than silently reconciled. The full issuer annual source supersedes a secondary snippet, while a clear dated secondary market row remains explicitly secondary. Open questions are the ₹9.09 crore gross presentation, legal setoff/deposit availability, current receivable collections and supplier terms, software commercialization/cost basis, actual rate-contract sub-POs/AMCmargin, post-March encumbrance and a full authenticated 60-session market/depth record. Reproduction verifies the retained calculations; it is not fresh authentication of unavailable originals or asset recoverability.

summary: Praruh is a fast-growing ICT systems integrator and equipment/services supplier, not yet a demonstrated proprietary software compounder. Its revenue and economic value added have genuinely expanded, and the IPO removed bank debt. The decisive concern is that FY26 growth converted into receivables and inventory rather than cash, with suppliers supplying most of the incremental funding. A related-party AI marketing agreement does not establish owned platform revenues. At the dated secondary reference of ₹139, reported earnings imply about 20.6× P/E, not an obviously distressed valuation. The conclusion is Hold — unresolved: a financing-sensitive growth watchlist, not an eligible purchase or compounder candidate. An explicit reconciliation of prior gross bank/deposit presentation, satisfactory collections and sustained funded execution would change the assessment; a cheaper quote alone would not.
